assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:annette-penrose@original-light-novels#86-annette-penrose-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-5 Annette Penrose character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence (its perfume-battle story excluded by the profile) and Alter.2 excluded. The profile states that its cumulative diagnostic index holds 185 rows (ANN-001 to ANN-185), that five rows reuse Phase-5 locators and the rest are LOCATOR_GAP rows, and that the index, not the prose, is the retrieval surface for exact Japanese anchors; the profile itself lists 23 highest-value controls by row range, routed by volume and usually XHTML file but never to a paragraph, three of them with a Phase-5 locator (V04-L015, V04-L033, V11-L003). That index is not curated evidence on this subject, and no row, count by volume or anchor is taken from it. The CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report, the relationship register matrix, other characters' profiles, the ledgers L01, L02 and L09, Documents 06, 08, 09, 12 and 18, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject either, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume, Alter.2 scene or other character's profile is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's developmental states from V01 through the V14 boundary: V01 selective care inside the Republic's dehumanizing asymmetry (p-005) and the inherited punishment logic revealed in the rupture with Lena (Vladilena Milizé) (p-014); V04 reunion and the collapse of the restoration script (p-006, with the challenge by Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) at V04-L015), split before and after the located fact that Shin (Shinei Nouzen) does not remember the quarrel as she assumed (p-012, V04-L033); V04-V06 new relation instead of restored childhood, ending with the リッタ return and the self-risk field experiment in V06 (p-005; the V06 experiment controls have no XHTML file); V07 jealousy coaching of Lena (p-008); V09 ordinary desire as a sufficient future (p-009); V11-V12 guilt corrigible rather than sovereign (V11 p-010, V11-L003; V12 p-004 and p-006); and V13-V14 belonging, nonvetoing care and live trauma (V13 p-003; V14 p-005, p-006/007 and p-008). V10 p-033 is prewar memory and counterfactual, not a present state. V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control. No default state is set; one must be selected. Alter.1 rows are supplements without volume placement, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Annette (Annette Penrose): a technically incisive, socially abrasive but attentive researcher whose central problem is not lack of conscience but the tendency to turn conscience into self-punishment, framed by the question of what she does when conscience, technical curiosity, friendship and the wish to punish herself point in different directions. It says what decides: she notices mechanism, institutional hypocrisy, social asymmetry and possible responsibility (the last as a stated bias producing false positives); she intervenes when she sees both preventable harm and a lever she can pull; under technical uncertainty she runs affect, causal connection, hypothesis, data demand and tasking (V12 p-004; V14 p-006/007); after failure she defaults to guilt and, in mature states, repairs when trusted others refuse the guilt logic (V11 p-010, V11-L003; V12 p-006). It separates accurate pessimism about available power from self-protective fatalism (V01 p-014) and predicts her mistakes: the V01 asymmetry that treats Eighty-Six risk as less significant (p-005), demanding that Shin (Shinei Nouzen) remember and respond so her atonement can complete (V04 p-006, p-012), inventing guilt beyond her causal standing, pushing too bluntly, and finding self-risk easier than externalized risk (V06). A would overclaim: the set is one derived artifact whose anchors sit in an uncurated index, the controls are routed only to file, V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control, and the profile rates the motive behind her self-risk and the generality of her privacy ethic only MODERATE. C would understate an account that says which consideration decides in each sampled class and predicts her overreach with its corrections.

The profile orders the development of Annette (Annette Penrose) with causes: V01 selective care with a racialized moral boundary (p-005) and punishment logic inherited from her father, Josef Penrose, whose maximum Para-RAID activation was suicide (p-014); V04 collapse of the restoration model when Shin (Shinei Nouzen) does not remember the betrayal (p-006; p-012, V04-L033); V04-V06 continuity without restoration, ending in the リッタ return and her reframing as the friend of Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and his present colleague (V06 p-005); V09 ordinary desire as a sufficient future (p-009); V11-V12 guilt corrected by Lena and refused by Theo (Theoto Rikka) (V11 p-010; V12 p-006); and V13-V14 routine tea with Theo, nonvetoing care and the father trauma reopened by Lena (V13 p-003; V14 p-005, p-008). It forbids two regressions: retroactively cleaning up V01, and treating guilt as gone rather than no longer sovereign. C would understate an ordered, causally explained sequence with located corrections. A is rejected: V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control, the V06 experiment controls have no file, no row is routed to a paragraph, and nothing after V14 is established.

The profile fixes the written-Japanese register of Annette (Annette Penrose): first person あたし as a strong default (私 in relaxed speech would sound too formal), familiar あんた, direct 何よ, だから？, でしょ, じゃない and ～なの, feminine ～わよ, ～のよ and ～かしら where natural, rough nouns (バカ, 奴, クズ) when irritated, and denser causal vocabulary in research without a change of personality. It gives directed address: レーナ and あんた with Lena (Vladilena Milizé), including 大嫌いよ、レーナ at the V01 rupture (p-014); ノウゼン大尉 and ペンローズ少佐 at reunion, then シン and リッタ with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (V04 p-006; V06 p-005), and アネットでも別にいいわよ in Alter.1 (part0056); アネットでいいわよ to Theo (Theoto Rikka) (V09 p-009) and the effortful 帰ってきてよ (V14 p-005); and 王子様 for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk). State deltas are stated: anger gets faster and more accusatory, guilt narrows and weakens the voice, and fear for a loved person removes the cleverness (V14 p-008). C would understate located morphology, address shifts and state rules. A is rejected: there is no frequency data, no exemplar has a paragraph route, the professional rank forms used when role distance matters are not specified, and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

The profile treats ordinary appetite as a stable part of Annette (Annette Penrose) that guilt colonized rather than replaced, and gives the driver as the later repermission of ordinary desire. Located ordinary conduct includes coffee and cake with Lena (Vladilena Milizé) (V01 p-005), pre-service shopping, fashion, jewelry and matching rabbit mugs (Alter.1 part0012), bringing films to injured soldiers (V09 p-009), routine tea with Theo (Theoto Rikka) (V13 p-003), the apology birthday gift to Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (Alter.1 part0056), the remade childhood cookie disaster (part0058) and her own birthday with Theo's gift (part0060). It states that her cooking is catastrophically bad, that gifts are a preferred way of making relations concrete, and that care need not look solemn. C would understate stated drivers with located conduct across the corpus. A is rejected: there is no routine or frequency, Alter.1 rows are not placed by volume, and several items (fashion preferences, gift choices, media taste) have no listed control of their own.

Eight directed relations of Annette (Annette Penrose) are analyzed with distinct registers: Lena (Vladilena Milizé), the most linguistically permissive tie, where care sounds like impatience and rupture can be cruel (V01 p-005, p-014; V07 p-008; V14 p-008); Shin (Shinei Nouzen), asymmetric with respect to guilt, moving from rank distance to negotiated present familiarity (V04 p-006, p-012; V06 p-005; Alter.1 part0050, part0056, part0058); Theo (Theoto Rikka), the ordinary-future and guilt-regulation partner (V09 p-009; V12 p-006; V13 p-003; V14 p-005); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), a defensive then morally checked relation that the profile says is narrow and stronger in the reverse direction (V04 p-006, V04-L015); Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), a technical peer for banter; Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), complementary technical expertise; Dustin, a fellow Republic survivor, shared context and ridicule (V11 p-014); and the Eighty-Six, a longitudinal dismantling of the V01 categorization. C would understate this partner-specific discrimination. A is rejected: Vika and Grethe have no listed control, Frederica is narrow by the profile's own statement, reverse directions are analyzed only for Frederica, and the relationship matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Annette (Annette Penrose) are located mainly through speech, conduct and highly visible embodied affect: the V01 confession of her betrayal of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) and her decision to bear her father's sin (p-014); the despair when Shin does not remember, with narration identifying the self-serving part of her wish to atone (V04 p-006); the residual, noncurrent childhood feeling (V07 p-008); prewar memory and an imagined warless counterfactual (V10 p-033); asking Theo (Theoto Rikka) to call her a traitor (V12 p-006); and crying relief when Lena (Vladilena Milizé) returns (V14 p-008). These states drive located choices. B would overclaim: the profile says her body makes internal state externally legible and classifies no exemplar as narration, inner speech or dialogue, most interior states are inferred from conduct, and the amount of romantic residue toward Shin after V07 is MODERATE in the profile. D would understate located admissions causally tied to her conduct.

The profile states the conflict style of Annette (Annette Penrose): she attacks the structure she thinks the other person is hiding behind (saintliness, qualification and self-erasure in Lena (Vladilena Milizé); hypocrisy in institutions; deservingness in herself), her anger gets louder and faster rather than silent (V01 p-014), she probes bluntly with repeated questions (V07 p-008), and she can push too hard when the other person needs space. Repair is often behavioral (changed conduct, privacy, practical help) as well as ごめん, and in mature states she accepts correction without needing to win (V11 p-010, V11-L003; V12 p-006). C would understate conditioned response families with located corrections. A is rejected: the V01 rupture is the one full-scale interpersonal conflict listed, conflict with formal superiors is not sampled, and the V04 exchange with Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) ends in her silence rather than a sampled resolution.

The profile gives Annette (Annette Penrose) argued positions with a failure mode: technical possibility, occurrence, use and permissibility are separate questions, and she brackets horror only for the diagnostic step before disgust returns when the abuse of children is established (V12 p-004); responsibility survives without entitlement to remembrance, hatred, forgiveness or punishment (V04 p-012, V04-L033); privacy can outrank institutional research completeness, as when she withholds the identity of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) as an ability-bearer (Alter.1 part0050); a self-experiment is preferable to externalized risk but may also be guilt-enabled (V06); and wanting Theo (Theoto Rikka) not to return does not give her a veto over his choice (V14 p-005). It keeps the V01 devaluation of Eighty-Six risk as an early state (p-005) and predicts the recurring error of treating suffering as proof of responsibility. C would understate located positions with a reasoning pattern and failure mode. A is rejected: the profile rates the generality of her privacy ethic and the motive behind her self-risk only MODERATE, the V06 experiment controls have no file, and her relation to the Republic as homeland is OPEN.

The profile gives the comic engines of Annette (Annette Penrose): sarcastic repetition (何がよ, だから？, V07 p-008), mean-looking jokes without mean intent (the remade cookies, Alter.1 part0058), social ambushes that make someone face what they avoid, technical deadpan, and shared ridicule as intimacy (the bonfire of Republic elite letters with Dustin, a fellow Republic survivor, V11 p-014). It bounds them: she is not universally hostile, and when she fears for a loved person the cleverness disappears (V14 p-008), so a witty Annette at that moment would be wrong. C would understate functional forms with located controls and a suspension condition. A is rejected: there is no stop rule for social ambushes beyond 'helpful or intrusive depending on context', technical deadpan and the V01 dissection joke have no listed control, and several forms rest on Alter.1 without volume placement.

A dedicated canonical profile of Annette (Annette Penrose) over V01-V14 and Alter.1. The profile says its index holds 185 rows, but it hands exact anchors to that uncurated index; in the set itself are 23 highest-value controls named by row range and routed to volume and usually XHTML file, never to a paragraph, three with a Phase-5 locator, and the V06 experiment controls with no file. V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control. C would overclaim: a reviewer cannot reach a single paragraph from the set, the listed controls are a subset whose rows are described only in grouped ranges, and the narrower authorities that govern conflicts (L01, L02, L09, Documents 06, 08, 09 and 12, and the matrix) are outside the set. E would understate a dedicated profile whose file-routed controls reach every developmental state it names across ten volumes and Alter.1.

For Annette (Annette Penrose) there are ten dispositioned counterexamples, ten mischaracterization traps and twenty would-sound-wrong constraints. Located negatives include the V01 devaluation of Eighty-Six risk (p-005) against any reading of her as enlightened from the start, Shin (Shinei Nouzen) genuinely not remembering the quarrel (V04 p-012, V04-L033), Lena (Vladilena Milizé) correcting invented guilt (V11 p-010, V11-L003), Theo (Theoto Rikka) refusing to condemn her (V12 p-006), the V13 narration denying that colleagues' teasing establishes a romance (p-003), her withholding of Shin's identity against the claim that curiosity makes her disclose anything (Alter.1 part0050), and the profile's own exclusion of the Alter.1 perfume battle as non-event. C would understate these affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: many constraints are profile rules without a listed control, and limits after V14 are open.

The developmental states of Annette (Annette Penrose) are each located by volume and, for listed controls, XHTML file, with order inside two volumes: V04 reunion and the Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) challenge (p-006) before the located fact that Shin (Shinei Nouzen) does not remember (p-012), and V14 the return of Theo (Theoto Rikka) to the front (p-005), the mental-disruption analysis (p-006/007) and the maximum-activation crisis of Lena (Vladilena Milizé) (p-008). B would overclaim: no control is routed to a paragraph, V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control, the V06 experiment has no file, V04-V06 is a grouped phase, and no default state is named. D would understate a seven-state sequence located by volume and file with in-volume order in V04 and V14 and three Phase-5 locators.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with あたし as the relaxed default and the attested blunt colloquial particles; 私 only where a marked professional context justifies it, and no invented rank formula.

Address uses only attested forms for the selected state: レーナ and あんた with Lena (Vladilena Milizé); ノウゼン大尉 at V04 reunion, シン thereafter, with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) able to call her リッタ from V06 and アネット offered in Alter.1; アネット invited from Theo (Theoto Rikka) from V09; 王子様 as banter for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk).
State is fixed before register: anger is fast and accusatory, guilt is small and narrowed, technical focus is Annette plus denser causal vocabulary, and fear for a loved person removes the wit.
No frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed, and output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains morphology, address shifts and state deltas enough for illustrative output with sampled relations. The absence of paragraph-located exemplars and frequency data restricts form and confidence rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected state; there is no default. The states are: V01 before the rupture with Lena (Vladilena Milizé) (p-005) or after the confession (p-014); V04 after reunion and before the located fact that Shin (Shinei Nouzen) does not remember (p-006), or after it (p-012); V06 after the リッタ return (p-005); V07 (p-008); V09 after the hospital conversation with Theo (Theoto Rikka) (p-009); V11-V12 after the corrections (V11 p-010; V12 p-006); V13 (p-003); or V14 before or after the maximum-activation crisis (p-008). V02, V03, V05 and V08 are not used, V10 p-033 is memory only, nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 rows do not fix a state.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Theo (Theoto Rikka), Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) only within the V04 exchange, or Dustin, a fellow Republic survivor, within shared Republic ridicule. Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) and Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) have no listed control and are a separate, lower-confidence condition, as is an unfamiliar colleague.

The situation matches a sampled class: an unfamiliar neural or Para-RAID mechanism, evidence of institutional abuse, a missed clue inviting self-blame, a friend evading a desire, a loved person choosing danger, ordinary food, coffee, fashion, gifts or media, or privacy of a person's research identity.

Output predicts her characteristic errors (early devaluation of Eighty-Six risk in V01, demanding that Shin remember, invented guilt, pushing too bluntly, accepting self-risk too easily) and never makes her an affectless analyst.
It abstains on any settled romance with Theo or Shin, her postwar career, and her final relation to the Republic; it introduces no institution, technology or relationship state absent from V01-V14.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected V01-V14 state at the located file-level turns: V01 p-005 or p-014; V04 p-006 or p-012; V06 p-005; V07 p-008; V09 p-009; V11 p-010 and V12 p-006; V13 p-003; V14 before or after p-008. No default, no V02, V03, V05 or V08 state, no state after V14, and no chronological use of Alter.1.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Shin (Shinei Nouzen) or Theo (Theoto Rikka) in their attested registers; Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) only within the V04 exchange; Dustin, a fellow Republic survivor, only within shared Republic ridicule. Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) and unfamiliar colleagues are a separate, lower-confidence transfer.

No V15+ setting, postwar career or Alter.2 scene

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected file-level state. Unlisted volumes, settled romance and postwar life are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: coffee and cake, shopping, fashion and jewelry, matching mugs and gifts, films and anime brought to friends, tea routines, birthdays, and catastrophically bad baking used as teasing.
Care is concrete and often teasing; ordinary wanting needs no grand justification in states from V09 on.
No invented daily routine, favorite list or civilian schooling beyond what the profile attests.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring located ordinary conduct with a stated driver supports bounded extrapolation. The absence of routine and frequency blocks READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: technical possibility against moral permission, responsibility without entitlement to the injured person's response, privacy against institutional completeness, self-risk against externalized risk, and care that refuses to veto another person's choice.
The selected state matters: in V01 she devalues Eighty-Six risk and treats suffering as owed; from V11 she can accept correction of guilt beyond her causal standing.
No decision about her relation to the Republic as homeland, and no postwar research ethics beyond these classes.
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions with a stated failure mode and located corrections support bounded ethical extrapolation within the sampled classes.

The profile affirmatively leaves romance open for Annette (Annette Penrose): V13 narration states that colleagues' teasing does not establish her relation with Theo (Theoto Rikka) as that kind of relationship (p-003), V14 adds stronger coding while leaving her own understanding unresolved, relationship status is OPEN, and 'Theo's girlfriend' and 'Shin's forgotten first love' are listed traps. The childhood feeling toward Shin (Shinei Nouzen) is residual and noncurrent (V07 p-008), and its present amount is MODERATE. CONDITIONAL would require settling what the profile leaves open.

conditions: Her role is the Para-RAID and neural-interface researcher: private warnings about unknown long-term risk (V01 p-005), the self-risk field experiment (V06), the illicit-implant hypothesis and record search (V12 p-004), and the mental-disruption Legion analysis ending in data and sample requests (V14 p-006/007).

Her domain is neural mechanism, information transfer, cognition and experimental inference, not vehicles or general engineering, which belong to Grethe (Grethe Wenzel); she distrusts official safety claims and protects private research identities.
No command authority, postwar career or institutional role outside the sampled research settings is modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled research reasoning with a stated sequence and ethical boundary supports bounded extrapolation within one selected state.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V01-V14 for Annette (Annette Penrose), with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. Her romantic outcome with Theo (Theoto Rikka), her postwar career, her final relation to the Republic and any later change in the ethical status of her research are OPEN in the profile.

The relation between Annette (Annette Penrose) and Theo (Theoto Rikka) is not established as a romance: V13 narration denies that colleagues' teasing settles it (p-003), and V14 leaves her own understanding unresolved.

The criticism by Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) that Annette (Annette Penrose) wants restoration rather than repair is that character's interpretation, not narration (V04 p-006, V04-L015), and guilt that Annette feels is not evidence of real responsibility (V11 p-010, V11-L003).

The profile of Annette (Annette Penrose) is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic Documents), none of which is curated on this row. It names its cumulative index as the retrieval surface for exact anchors; that index is not curated here.

No listed control for Annette (Annette Penrose) is routed to a paragraph, the V06 experiment controls have no XHTML file, and V02, V03, V05 and V08 have no listed control, so states in those volumes cannot be selected.
The profile does not classify any exemplar for Annette (Annette Penrose) as narration, inner speech or dialogue, and most of her private states are read from speech, conduct and visible affect.
The profile makes no claim about pitch, prosody or performed voice for Annette (Annette Penrose); voice claims cover written Japanese only.
